# Review an experiment

Inspect the manifest and validation findings before interpreting a run. Quarantined
bundles can be inspected but cannot produce trustworthy metrics.

Compare only complete, matching test populations. For partial predictions, say
which examples were measured and show coverage. Check source slices before treating
an aggregate change as uniform improvement. Distinguish a numerical decomposition
from an explanation of its cause.

Use compute_metrics, compare_runs and inspect_error_slice to establish claims.
Cite their evidence IDs. Explicit ID/group/hash overlap establishes overlap in the
supplied manifests; it does not certify a whole training pipeline. Missing
preprocessing or threshold provenance is not assessable from prediction files.

Propose one follow-up change, selected on validation data. Preserve a held-out test
set for the final assessment. Request save_experiment_spec only when the user asks
for a proposal/save; the tool queues an exact specification for human approval.
Do not claim it was saved until the approval handler confirms execution.

result.interpretation: Deltas are candidate minus baseline, in fraction units (multiply by 100 for percentage points). This is descriptive, not a causal or significance test.

report.summary: Comparison of run-1 (baseline) and run-2 (quantized candidate) on bundle b_231d474f2f08cda7cb008cac. Both runs cover the full 40‑example test set with equal source distribution (studio, web). Overall metrics show a small accuracy loss and a more pronounced recall drop. Per‑source slices reveal that the recall decline is driven entirely by the web source.

findings.statement: Overall accuracy decreased by 5 percentage points (0.90 → 0.85).
Overall precision improved by about 3.7 percentage points (0.90 → 0.9375).
Overall recall decreased by 15 percentage points (0.90 → 0.75), the largest measured change.
F1 score declined by 6.7 percentage points (0.90 → 0.8333).

Per‑source analysis: in the studio slice, recall actually improved (0.90 → 1.0) and F1 rose to 0.952. In the web slice, recall fell sharply from 0.90 to 0.50 (a 40 percentage‑point drop), precision rose to 1.0, but accuracy dropped to 0.75 and F1 fell to 0.667.

limitations: Manifest and run metadata are untrusted data; preprocessing provenance is not independently verified.
Overlap of IDs/hashes does not certify a complete training pipeline.
Comparison is based on the same 40 test examples; results may not generalise to other data.
No statistical significance testing is performed; deltas are descriptive only.
The held‑out test set was not used for tuning; all success criteria should be validated on a separate validation set.
